title: Merkle tree (hash tree)
summary: A Merkle tree is a binary tree where each leaf is a hash of a data block, and each internal node is a hash of its children. The root hash (Merkle root) summarizes all data. Used for data integrity verification, blockchain (Bitcoin, Ethereum), Git (commit graph), and distributed systems (Cassandra, IPFS).

structure.meaning: Hash of a data block (e.g., SHA-256 of a 4KB block).
Hash of (left child hash || right child hash). For odd number of leaves, duplicate the last leaf.
Top of the tree. Summarizes all data blocks.
To prove a leaf is in the tree, provide the leaf and the sibling hashes along the path to the root (Merkle proof).
Recompute the path from the leaf to the root using the provided siblings. Compare with the expected root.

notes: Merkle trees are the foundation of blockchain (Bitcoin, Ethereum).
Merkle proofs allow light clients to verify data without downloading the full chain.
Git uses a Merkle tree-like structure for its object graph (commit -> tree -> blob).
Merkle trees are used in Cassandra (anti-entropy repair), IPFS (content addressing), and Certificate Transparency.
Patricia tries (Merkle-Patricia) are used in Ethereum for state storage.
